Real, but minor given the persistent-failure trigger.

votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) "Every retraction path in this function already has retry-then-drop semantics, so this is nothing new" — partially true, but the pre-existing paths only fail when the retraction's own dependencies (stamphog product DB, GitHub) fail; the carve-out inserts main-DB tables, the tasks facade and the review_hog resolver in front of the retraction, so a failure isolated to those now drops a dismissal that would have succeeded. (2) "The carve-out only does DB work for bot-authored repo-native PRs" (tasks.py:168-179) — true, which narrows the blast radius to self-driving inbox PRs, but those are exactly the PRs that now carry stamphog approvals and can be pushed to. (3) "A draft cannot be merged, so the stale approval is harmless" — the design explicitly lets the draft-time approval carry over the ready_for_review flip (161-163) and that flip is not a retraction point (49), so the stale approval reaches a mergeable state. (4) "The next delivery heals it" — only a synchronize/reopened after recovery does; no sweep exists. (5) Existing tests — none cover a raising carve-out. None of the refutations hold. Severity is should_fix rather than must_fix because the trigger needs a persistent (>~15s) failure confined to the carve-out chain on a previously approved inbox PR, which is rare, and the fix is small (fail closed to `_InboxCarveOut()` on the final attempt, or run the head-changing retraction before the carve-out).

votes.evidence:
Ordering is new and as described. PR #75215's diff for products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py shows the old skip path went straight from `skip_reason = _review_skip_reason(pr)` (payload-only) to `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip(skip_repo_config, pr, _UNTRUSTED_SKIP_DISMISS_MESSAGE)`; the head now interposes `_inbox_rereview_carve_out(...)` inside a raise-and-retry wrapper at /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:871-879, and the head-changing retraction sits after it at tasks.py:887-903. The task is `@shared_task(max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5)` (tasks.py:809), so a carve-out exception that persists across four attempts (~15-20s) fails the task before the retraction runs; the delivery is never marked processed, and GitHub does not redeliver on its own.

The carve-out adds dependencies the retraction does not have. For a bot-authored, repo-native, head-changing delivery on an enabled synced config it calls `find_signal_implementation_run` (tasks.py:190-195) -> `find_task_run` on `TaskRun`, a plain `models.Model` on the main DB (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/models.py:1063; the `tasks` app is not in products/db_routing.yaml), then the review_hog resolver: `SignalReportArtefact` (main DB, /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:180-186), `resolve_org_github_login_to_users` over `Team`/`OrganizationMembership`/`UserSocialAuth`/`UserIntegration`/`Integration`/`User` (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/signals/backend/report_generation/resolve_reviewers.py:313-331, 355-380; only `Team.DoesNotExist` is caught), and `ReviewUserSettings.load` (main DB, /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/models.py:311-314). The retraction itself only needs `StamphogRepoConfig`/`PullRequest`/`ReviewRun` on the stamphog product DB (products/db_routing.yaml routes app `stamphog` to database `stamphog`; tasks.py:298-304, 501-506; /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/logic/approvals.py:44-53) plus the GitHub API.

The trigger is reachable in production. Self-driving inbox PRs are bot-authored drafts on the team's own repo (tasks.py:169-171, 866), `process_inbox_pr_review` queues a stamphog run with `inbox_review` provenance, the workflow passes `self_driving_review=True` to the engine (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451) and can `post_approve_review` (activities.py:745), so a standing stamphog approval on such a PR exists; every later `synchronize` on it enters the guarded carve-out. review_hog is installed and registers the resolver at startup (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/posthog/settings/web.py:76; receivers.py:58-69). No test exercises a raising carve-out: products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:762-880 patch `_FIND_RUN`/`_RESOLVER_SLOT` with returning stubs only.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) "The carve-out returns early for most PRs" - true for human PRs (`_is_bot_authored` gate, tasks.py:169-171), but self-driving PRs are bot-authored by construction, so the exact PRs whose approvals the retraction protects are the ones that run the fallible chain. (2) "Both paths share the same DB, so an outage blocks the retraction anyway" - the stamphog app is routed to its own `stamphog` database in products/db_routing.yaml, while `TaskRun`, `SignalReportArtefact`, `ReviewUserSettings` and the org/user tables live on the main DB; I could not read the production env to confirm `PRODUCT_DB_STAMPHOG_WRITER_URL` is set, and if stamphog shares the main DB in prod the outage trigger becomes moot (only a persistent code-path exception in the new chain would still block the retraction). (3) "Another sweep catches it" - the only other dismissal is the workflow activity (activities.py:290), which needs a review run, and the next `synchronize` sweep, so the stale approval stands until the next push or run. (4) "A draft can't be merged" - true, which narrows the blast radius: harm needs a push during the failure, then a `ready_for_review` flip (not head-changing, so no retraction there either, per the docstring at tasks.py:160-163), then a human merge relying on the stale approval. The failure needs a main-DB read failure or resolver exception lasting through four attempts in ~20s, coinciding with a push to an approved self-driving PR, followed by that multi-step path; the fix is small (fail-closed carve-out, or run the generic retraction before the carve-out), but the coincidence is rare enough that I rate it consider rather than the validator's should_fix.
